frames.narration: A service publishes an event with the key order-42. It hashes the key and picks partition 2, then sends a batch to that partition's leader with its producer id 9 and the sequence number 7 for this partition.

The leader checks that sequence 7 follows the last one it saw from producer 9, which was 6, and appends the event to its log at offset 1,204. The log now ends at offset 1,205, but the event is not yet visible to consumers.
The two followers fetch from the leader as if they were consumers. Each writes the event to its own log and reports its position, so the leader knows that all three replicas have offset 1,204.

Every member of the in-sync set has the event, so the high watermark moves to 1,205 and the event is committed. With acks=all the leader acknowledges the producer. This acknowledgement is lost on the way.

The producer times out and sends the same batch again with the same producer id and sequence 7. The leader sees that 7 is not above the last sequence it stored, so it writes nothing and acknowledges again. There is exactly one copy of the event.

A consumer in the group that owns partition 2 polls from its position, 1,204. The leader returns events up to the high watermark and no further, so the consumer can never read an event that a leader crash could still erase.

The consumer processes the event, then commits offset 1,205, the next one to read, by writing it to the offsets topic, which is itself a replicated, compacted log. If this member dies now, whichever member takes over partition 2 resumes at 1,205.
